claims.text: An MTP-based perturbation scheme can replace full-phase-space ab initio thermodynamic integration and accurately calculate phase-decomposition free-energy differences in a Ta-based refractory BCC high-entropy alloy.
The MTP training set must explicitly contain SRO configurations and ordered clusters to achieve the claimed accuracy.
Including SRO and ordered-cluster configurations avoids the failure mode of potentials that assume a random solid solution.
The initial Ta-based refractory BCC alloy is a disordered random solid solution at high temperature before phase decomposition.
Temperatures of 1500–2500 K are near the melting point or phase-transition region of the target alloy.
Accurate phase-transition calculations require the potential to reproduce the energy cost of breaking local chemical order through diffuse antiphase-boundary formation.
SRO and B2-like ordered clusters mediate free-energy differences and phase stability.
Standard EAM potentials fail to capture the energy penalty associated with breaking local chemical order and creating diffuse antiphase boundaries.
An MTP trained on ab initio configurations containing SRO can correctly model the Gibbs free-energy landscape.
The proposed perturbation scheme can resolve subtle free-energy differences between random and SRO or ordered phases without full ab initio sampling.
The MTP scheme will predict a stable B2+BCC two-phase state or an SRO-stabilized microstructure where EAM predicts a single-phase random solid solution.
Replacing half of the Co with Cr in AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi induces B2+BCC phase separation even after annealing at 1000 °C.
Experimental or simulation trends in similar multicomponent alloys establish SRO stabilization relevant to the predicted Ta-alloy phase behavior.
The MTP-based scheme will reduce computational cost by orders of magnitude relative to full DFT thermodynamic integration.
EAM calculations and ab initio thermodynamic integration based on a random-solution assumption typically overestimate the stability of the disordered phase in multicomponent refractory alloys.
An MTP trained only on random configurations will fail to capture the SRO energy penalty and will reproduce EAM-like artifacts.
Existing machine-learning potentials have limitations in representing complex multicomponent liquid structures without extensive validation.
The cited evidence does not characterize a specific TOR-TILD failure mode in high-dimensional multicomponent chemical space.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says full-phase-space thermodynamic integration is replaced by a perturbation scheme, but the intervention includes thermodynamic integration through a coupling parameter as an example. Coupling-parameter integration may still be thermodynamic integration, so the claimed replacement is not consistently distinguished from a cheaper implementation of the same method.
